title: A clinical trial to study how well VVD-133214, in combination with another anticancer drug called pembrolizumab, works in people with advanced cancer of the colon or rectum
official: (VVD-133214-02 / 23236) A Phase 2, Randomized, Open-label Study of VVD-133214 in Combination with Pembrolizumab compared to Pembrolizumab Monotherapy in Participants with Advanced Colorectal Adenocarcinoma (CRC) Harboring Microsatellite Instability (MSI) and/or Deficient Mismatch Repair (DMMR)
summary: Main objective: To evaluate the efficacy of VVD-133214 in combination with pembrolizumab compared to pembrolizumab monotherapy

interventions.name: KEYTRUDA 25 mg/mL concentrate for solution for infusion

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Age ≥ 18 years on the date of signing informed consent
2. Females of childbearing potential must have negative serum pregnancy test before starting study treatment
3. Life expectancy of at least 12 weeks
4. Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance-status score of 0 or 1
5. Have a known microsatellite instability (MSI) and/or deficient mismatch repair (dMMR) tumor status confirmed per local standard of care (SoC), and have histologically or cytologically documented advanced (unresectable and/or metastatic) colorectal adenomarcinoma (CRC)
6. No prior systemic treatment for metastatic disease and not amenable to curative resection
7. Participants must have documented MSI and/or dMMR tumor status determined as part of the routine diagnostic workup in a certified laboratory
8. Availability of formaldehyde-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) archival tumor tissue for submission to Sponsor/central laboratory for retrospective central testing including a copy of a redacted pathology report if available
9. Presence of measurable disease according to RECIST v1.1
10. Adequate hematologic and end-organ function, defined using the following laboratory results obtained within 14 days prior to first dose of study treatment - Adequate hematological status (Neutrophils ≥ 1500/μL; Platelets ≥ 100,000/μL; Hemoglobin ≥ 9.0 g/dL;  - Adequate renal function: Creatinine clearance ≥ 50 ml/min (Cockcroft and Gault);  - Adequate liver function: Serum bilirubin ≤ 1.5 x upper normal limit (ULN); Alanine aminotransferase (ALT) ≤ 2.5 x ULN; Aspartate aminotransferase (AST) ≤ 2.5 x ULN; Participants with documented liver metastases: AST and ALT ≤ 5 × ULN; Hemostasis: Prothrombin time (PT)/International normalized ratio (INR) and activated partial PT (aPTT) ≤ 1.5 x ULN (Participants receiving therapeutic anticoagulation should be on a stable dose for at least 1 week prior to C1D1)
Exclusion criteria:
1. Prior systemic treatment for advanced CRC. Participants may have received prior adjuvant chemotherapy as long as disease progression occurred at least 12 months after the last dose of adjuvant treatment.
2. Prior treatment with any WRN helicase inhibitor
3. Prior treatment with adjuvant immunotherapy (eg, anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1, anti-PD-L2 agent, or anti-CTLA-4 agent, or any other antibody or drug specifically targeting T cell co-stimulation or immune checkpoint pathways, including prior therapy with anti-tumor vaccines or other immuno-stimulatory antitumor agents, etc).
4. Known active or uncontrolled central nervous system (CNS) or brain metastases (progressing or requiring anticonvulsants or corticosteroids for symptomatic control) and/or carcinomatous meningitis.
5. Patients with active or history of autoimmune disease or immune deficiency that has required treatment in past 2 years (Participants with a history of autoimmune-related hypothyroidism who are on thyroid replacement hormone are eligible for the study. Participants with controlled Type 1 diabetes mellitus who are on an insulin regimen are eligible for the study).
6. History of malignancy other than CRC, within 5 years prior to screening (exception: adequately treated carcinoma in situ of the cervix, non-melanoma skin carcinoma, localized prostate cancer (Gleason score Grade < 7), superficial urinary bladder cancer, ductal carcinoma in situ. Participants with Lynch syndrome are not excluded)
7. Participants requiring treatment with systemic immunosuppressive medication (such as corticosteroids) within 2 weeks prior to initiation of study treatment, or anticipation of need for systemic immunosuppressive medication during study treatment, with the following exceptions: inhaled or acute, low-dose steroid doses (such as <10 mg daily prednisone or equivalent are permitted)
8. Positive test for hepatitis B virus (HBV; defined as positive for hepatitis B surface antigen and/or positive for hepatitis B core antibody) or hepatitis C virus (HCV; defined as positive for HCV antibody or HCV RNA) per local diagnostic standard and in accordance with local laws and regulations, indicating acute or chronic infection. Participants who are positive for hepatitis C antibody may be eligible to participate if they have received a complete course of curative anti-viral therapy and have at least two negative HCV PCR tests immediately prior to trial participation.
9. Participants with known Werner Syndrome (WRN)
10. Treatment-related toxicities from prior cancer therapy that have not resolved to Grade ≤ 1 CTCAE prior to study treatment (exception: Grade 2 toxicities: alopecia, peripheral neuropathy, any clinically non-significant laboratory changes as determined by the Investigator and medical monitor)
